security_spec.violation_condition: In XiangShan RTL, any CLIC/IMSIC preemption threshold comparator that directly transcribes the old spec formula 'iprio[i] & NIPPRIO_MASK >= xithreshold' into Chisel/Verilog with HDL-native operator precedence will produce: iprio[i] & (NIPPRIO_MASK >= xithreshold). Since NIPPRIO_MASK is a wide constant (e.g., 0xFF for 8-bit priority) and xithreshold is a CSR-programmed small value, (NIPPRIO_MASK >= xithreshold) is a constant true, reducing the preemption condition to 'iprio[i] != 0' — any non-zero-priority pending interrupt preempts the current handler regardless of the threshold CSR value. Specifically in XiangShan's InterruptFilter, the IpriosSort/minSelect infrastructure at lines 162-189 performs priority comparison (prioNum <= comparison) but feeds into external IMSIC hardware (marked 'Todo: IMSIC' at CSRAIA.scala:197). If that external IMSIC threshold comparator uses the buggy precedence, the xithreshold CSR becomes non-functional for preemption gating.
security_spec.summary: Operator precedence bug in CLIC preemption formula (PR #633): iprio[i] & NIPPRIO_MASK >= xithreshold evaluates as iprio[i] & (NIPPRIO_MASK >= xithreshold) in HDL, turning xithreshold into a no-op and allowing unconditional preemption from any non-zero priority interrupt

findings.finding: The minSelect recursive priority comparator performs pure prioNum comparison at line 179 (Mux(left.prioNum <= right.prioNum, left, right)) with no preemption threshold qualification. This is the locus where a Smnip threshold comparator (IPRIO & NIPPRIO_MASK >= xithreshold) would be added. If implemented using the spec's raw formula without explicit Scala parentheses, Chisel's operator precedence would parse 'iprio & MASK >= threshold' as 'iprio & (MASK >= threshold)', which is constant-true, reducing preemption gating to 'iprio != 0'. Currently compliant because no threshold CSR wiring exists, but this is a high-risk insertion point for the described vulnerability class.
findings.snippet:
(!left.isZero && !right.isZero) -> Mux1H(Seq(
  (left.greaterThan255 && !right.greaterThan255) -> right,
  (!left.greaterThan255 && right.greaterThan255) -> left,
  (!left.greaterThan255 && !right.greaterThan255) -> Mux(left.prioNum <= right.prioNum, left, right),
))

spec_citations.excerpt: When xithreshold is a nonzero value, an interrupt source is considered disabled irrespective of its interrupt-enable bit, when the following condition holds: IPRIO >= xithreshold & NIPPRIO_MASK

findings.finding: The IpriosSort bundle (idx, enable, isZero, greaterThan255, prioNum) lacks threshold comparison fields (e.g., belowThreshold, exceedsThreshold). Adding a threshold field computed as 'prioNum & NIPPRIO_MASK >= mithreshold' without explicit parenthesization '(prioNum & NIPPRIO_MASK) >= mithreshold' would introduce the operator-precedence bug. Currently compliant by absence of any threshold logic.
findings.snippet:
class IpriosSort extends Bundle {
  val idx = UInt(6.W)
  val enable = Bool()
  val isZero = Bool()
  val greaterThan255 = Bool()
  val prioNum = UInt(8.W)
}

findings.finding: mipriosSort correctly extracts IPRIO fields from miprios CSR array (line 83: 'iprio.prioNum := miprios(7+8*defaultPrio, 8*defaultPrio)') and from mtopei.IPRIO (line 79). Enable is gated on mie bits via mtopigather (line 73). No threshold coparison exists here. Compliant for current non-Smnip state.

Per-privilege-level interrupt vector gating uses only privilege mode and xIE state bits (mstatusMIE/sstatusSIE/vsstatusSIE). No Smnip threshold qualification. Compliant for current non-Smnip architecture, but would need threshold qualification if Smnip is implemented.
findings.snippet:
val mIRVecTmp = Mux(
  privState.isModeM && mstatusMIE || privState < PrivState.ModeM,
  io.out.mtopi.IID.asUInt, 0.U)

findings.finding: Interrupt-level arbitration is purely privilege-mode-based (M > HS > VS) with hard ordering. No Smnip threshold-based preemption that would allow a lower-level interrupt to preempt a higher-level handler. Compliant for current non-Smnip state.
findings.snippet:
val irToHS = !mIRNotZero && hsIRNotZero
val irToVS = !mIRNotZero && !hsIRNotZero && vsIRNotZero

findings.finding: InterruptFilterIO input bundle lacks threshold CSR fields (mithreshold, mipreemptcfg.preemptmsk, mpistatus.pithreshold) and current-handler-priority fields required for Smnip nested preemption. Adding these fields without proper wiring from CSR modules would result in uninitialized/implicit-zero wires, making the threshold gate always-pass. Integration risk if Smnip CSRs are added.

spec_citations.excerpt: 0x347 mithreshold Interrupt enable threshold; 0x348 mipreemptcfg Interrupt preemption configuration

findings.finding: The AIA CSR module list (aiaCSRMods) registers mtopei/mtopi/stopei/stopi/vstopei/vstopi but no mithreshold or mipreemptcfg CSR modules. If Smnip CSRs are added to this list but omitted from aiaCSRMap/aiaCSROutMap (lines 175-181), or conversely added as modules but their outputs left unwired to InterruptFilterIO, the threshold CSR would be a dead write-only register with no effect on interrupt preemption. Integration risk.
findings.snippet:
val aiaCSRMods = Seq(
  miselect, mireg, mtopei, mtopi,
  siselect, sireg, stopei, stopi,
  vsiselect, vsireg, vstopi, vstopei,
)
